newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela needs two years for plane safety upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela needs two years for plane safety upgrade.

text.p: Venezuela said on Wednesday it would need nearly two years to meet U.S. Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) air safety standards after narrowly escaping a complete ban on its carriers at U.S. airports.

U.S. officials said on Tuesday there had already been "significant" improvements in Venezuelan air safety standards and that the country would be kept on a probationary FAA Category 2 rating in the meantime.

"With the FAA's help, and if we continue with our plans, Venezuela will be promoted to Category 1 ... in some 18 months to two years," Transport and Communications Minister Moises Orozco said after a weekly cabinet meeting.
But "it's won't be an easy or simple task."
Venezuela narrowly escaped a demotion to Category 3 when four planes were detained in Miami in August after failing FAA inspections.

The demotion would have barred Venezuelan planes from landing in the U.S. But Orozco, who was appointed minister in July, successfully extended Venezuela's Category 2 rating after meeting with U.S. transport officials in Washington.
The FAA "will be helping us with training and assessment so that we can successfully return category 1," he said.
